title: Mozambique follow-up agricultural evidence
purpose: Extend existing CAP 2023/24 evidence with INE producer-price and livestock tables, current provincial market reference quotations, and the newly identified CAP district-table archive. No calculator data are activated by this follow-up.

quality_notes: Table 3.1.6 explicitly labels the values average producer prices and attributes them to MADER/SIMA. The extracted HTML table does not expose the unit; do not assume MZN/kg until the original PDF page confirms it.
The national price series is not provincial and cannot alone represent province-specific farmgate receipts or seasonal grades.
Feijão Nhemba is cowpea; Feijão Manteiga and Feijão Boer are separate beans and must not be merged into the cowpea profile.
Livestock inventories are population context, not production, liveweight, sale prices, feed costs or gross margins.
The sheep series changes sharply from 1,101,488 in 2022 to 225,495 in 2023 and 239,206 in 2024; retain a data-quality flag.

quality_notes: These are provincial reference market averages transcribed by a secondary publication from ICM tables; they are not automatically farmgate prices.
The ICM table distinguishes rice from paddy rice; retain the exact product label and do not mix processed rice with paddy.
Maize in Inhambane and Maputo is identified as white maize; product grade differences matter.
The source's province collection periods can vary; do not treat the table as a single synchronous nationwide quotation.

findings.topic: Official SIMA data collection method and public access limitation
findings.source: Ministry of Agriculture, Environment and Fisheries (MAAP), Agricultural Market Information System
observations: SIMA states it has collected agricultural prices since 1991 and conducts weekly collection at producer, wholesale and retail levels.
Covered products include maize, rice, groundnuts, beans, horticulture and animal products; SIMA also records transport costs and wholesale availability.

Weekly Quente-Quente bulletins are the intended publication channel, but the public archive surfaced on the ministry page is largely older editions (including 2023), so current weekly producer-level data were not publicly extractable through this route.

findings.topic: INE Basic Indicators of Agriculture and Food 2025
observations: The 2025 publication and PDF download are confirmed on the official INE page.
The PDF did not yield readable table content in this review; no numerical values from it are admitted.

decision.reason: The newly extracted national producer-price series lacks a confirmed unit in the accessible table text and is not provincial; current ICM quotations are market references rather than confirmed farmgate transactions. District CAP tables and 2025 indicators still need extraction, and farmer-paid input, labour, irrigation, machinery and enterprise budgets remain missing.

next_actions: Inspect original Statistical Yearbook PDF page 66 to confirm producer-price unit and footnotes, then extract all crop rows and assess whether national values are appropriate for screening only.
Download and extract the official CAP district ZIP; cross-check provincial crop productivity and table 4.23 against district crop area, production, denominators and sampling/coverage notes.
Extract INE Basic Indicators of Agriculture and Food 2025 tables and reconcile with CAP and yearbook definitions.
Obtain current SIMA weekly Quente-Quente producer-level bulletins or an authorized raw data extract; preserve province, market, date, grade, unit and transaction level.
Verify ICM provincial market references against the original ICM bulletin and retain separate market/producer/wholesale/retail classifications.
Obtain farmer-paid seed, fertilizer, pesticide, labour, machinery hire, irrigation/pumping energy, transport and post-harvest costs by province and production system.
Build separate commercial enterprise budgets and validate all 17 calculator commodity mappings before activation.
safeguards: Do not alter original 10 active profiles or calculator formulas.
Do not equate smallholder CAP averages with commercial enterprise yields.
Do not treat market reference quotations as farmgate transactions.
Do not merge distinct bean species into the cowpea profile.
Do not infer units missing from source tables.
Do not activate Mozambique or publish a calculator test URL until data and regression tests pass.
